env_gates.APP_ENV: no direct gate; refuse-to-boot alignment enforced elsewhere

side_effects_on_startup: _emergency_prune_backups(): fs deletion of local backup zips only when disk >= high-watermark
asyncio.create_task(asset_spine_nightly_loop(db)): schedule nightly R2 asset spine reconciliation
await asyncio.sleep(1.5): give the task a moment to settle
if _backup_task.done(): _backup_task.result() → raises to surface early failure

r2_touch_points.r2_indirection_summary: R2 uploads happen inside `_backup_scheduler_loop` when a scheduled slot fires. Loop is singleton-locked and respects SCHEDULER_ENABLED. No R2 call occurs at startup registration.
r2_touch_points.asset_spine_nightly_loop: Reads Mongo, performs asset spine reconciliation; R2 side effects gated by service-level env flags.

email_touch_points.failure_alert_email_path: OUT OF SCOPE — lives in `_start_backup_verification_cron` (email-scheduler group, Track 22.1H, already migrated & fingerprint-locked) and inside the backup loop which routes through `_dispatch_auto_email` under EMAIL_SAFETY_MODE=strict.

trust_spine_touch_points.in_loop: Trust Spine audit rows may be emitted by the backup verification cron path; unaffected by this migration.

must_run_after: index-ensure (Mongo indexes exist so singleton-lock read/write is fast; not strict — lock is idempotent)
seed (unrelated but ordered earlier in previous topology; not strict)
safe_to_migrate_reasoning: Handler is env-gated by DISABLE_BACKUP_SCHEDULER for full opt-out.
All R2 work occurs inside the singleton-locked loop, not during registration.
Boot validation `await asyncio.sleep(1.5)` is preserved verbatim.
Supervisor task creation is preserved verbatim (fire-and-forget).
No handler in `on_startup` or `LIFECYCLE_STEPS` depends on this handler having run first (the loop wakes on cadence, not immediately).

The 3 remaining legacy on_startup handlers (command_center._startup, this, readiness-flip) will drop to 2 after cutover. Readiness-flip stays LAST via source-order preservation — it is still the LAST `@app.on_event('startup')` in server.py.
